critique.paragraph: This plate teaches Edge D (classification/identity-slippage), not Edge E (embodiment/continuous-discrete). The three dress mannequins read as discrete identity categories awaiting selection — a taxonomy problem, not an embodiment problem. Edge E requires visible tension between continuous body and discrete algorithm: Muybridge frames, quantized motion trails, gait snapped to grid cells. Here, the grid is mere background and the dresses are static objects. The player's VR body — the continuous element — is absent from the diagram. The visual grammar says 'choose your category' when it should say 'watch your motion get quantized.'
strengths: Grid substrate is visually strong and clearly algorithmic
Three-option spatial layout is legible from all angles
Clean composition with good label hierarchy
weaknesses: No continuous element visible — no motion, no gesture, no analogue body
Static mannequins cannot teach embodiment; they are objects, not bodies in motion
The continuous-discrete tension is entirely absent
Player's VR body (the actual continuous element) is not part of the spatial argument
Reads as 'which box do you fit in' (Edge D) not 'your body doesn't fit the algorithm' (Edge E)
next_gen_hints: Show VR hand trails being snapped to grid vertices in real-time — make the quantization visible
Add chronophotographic overlay: a walking figure split into discrete frames along the grid, Muybridge-style
Replace static dresses with motion-capture skeleton sequences showing continuous gesture quantized to discrete poses
Add temporal strip on wall: smooth sine wave of body motion above, stepped/pixelated version below
Make grid cells light up when player crosses them — show mismatch between smooth VR locomotion and discrete cell activation
Consider: player's own body captured as Marey-style composite — continuous motion frozen into one multi-exposure frame
Reframe 'outfit' as motion signature: show how continuous dance gets classified into discrete movement archetypes (Classical Gait, Wicked Stride, Custom Glitch)
